research_question: What is the effect of atorvastatin, compared with placebo or no treatment, on withdrawal due to adverse effects in adults?
outcome_description: Withdrawal or treatment discontinuation due to adverse effects or adverse events
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates higher rates of withdrawal due to adverse effects in the atorvastatin group compared to the control group.
search_queries: atorvastatin placebo adverse effects withdrawal randomized trial
atorvastatin discontinuation adverse events controlled trial
atorvastatin placebo discontinuation adverse effects clinical study
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies evaluating atorvastatin compared with placebo or no treatment in adult participants
Studies reporting quantitative data on participant withdrawal or treatment discontinuation due to adverse effects
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between atorvastatin and a placebo or no-treatment control condition
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size (event counts, proportions, risk ratios, or odds ratios of adverse event withdrawals required)
Completely unrelated to the research topic or conducted exclusively in pediatric populations
moderators_to_extract: clinical population / baseline indication (e.g., primary vs secondary cardiovascular prevention)
effect_size_note: Binary event outcome typically analyzed via relative risk, odds ratio, or risk difference.
